<!-- Title: "Decide whether…" or "Decide which…", in plain words. Write it so the person can answer in one word.
Never ask an open question ("thoughts?") when a choice can be offered. The standard:
https://github.com/moraph-com/mainspring/blob/main/docs/work-tracking-writing-standard.md, sections 4.5 and 6.3 ("Request for a person"). -->

## Status at a glance

| | |
|---|---|
| **Last updated** | YYYY-MM-DD |
| **What is happening now** | Waiting for the decision below. |
| **Next step** | Who decides, and by when. |
| **Waiting on a person?** | Yes: who, for what, by when |
| **Outlook** | What the deadline protects, in one sentence. |

## The question

One sentence, answerable with a choice.

## Decision needed from

@name, by Day D Month YYYY.

## Background

Two or three sentences. Assume the person has not read anything else.

## Options

| Option | What happens | Cost / risk |
|--------|--------------|-------------|
| A | | |
| B | | |

## My recommendation

Option [x], because [reason].

## If nobody decides by the deadline

What will happen by default, and why that is the safer or reversible choice. Or: "the work waits, because this cannot
be undone."

## To answer

Reply to this issue with "A" or "B".

## Related work

- Part of: #parent (one line on how)

## Technical details

For engineers. A non-technical reader can stop above this line.
